state:
**Goal `disconnect-completes`, Stage 3 in progress: a dropped request runs to its end under its `wall_time`, or under `disconnect_grace` while it has none, and a listed method is cancelled.** `Peer` in `crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs` carries `cancels`, the `grace` and the request tree's `SafepointView`, all read at the request's start. Its drop hangs the body supply up, then abandons (a listed method, the grace passed with no `wall_time` standing, the drain period's end, this task cancelled or torn down) or parks until the request ends.

The tree publishes the request's `wall_time` (`TreeState::wall_time`, written by `Ctx::publish_wall_time` from `refresh_limits` on the tree root and on the context answering the request). The waiting `Peer` files a one-shot `RemoteWake` in `TreeState::wall_time_watch`, so a `Core\Config::set` or `::restore` that moves `wall_time` wakes it at once.

Green now: every test of `nvs-server-a-disconnect-completes-the-request-by-default` except `the_drain_waits_for_a_disconnected_request` and `a_disconnected_request_runs_its_after_response_work`, which are not written. The rule stays `designed` until the stream write lands.

items.text: **`the_drain_waits_for_a_disconnected_request` and `a_disconnected_request_runs_its_after_response_work`** (`rule:http-server/a-request-outlives-a-client-that-goes-away`): the drop's wait already cuts at the drain period's end; check that a drain which begins while the task is parked in the drop wakes it, and write both tests through `after_a_disconnect` — `crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs:1013`, `crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs:6164`.

**A listed method whose body failed part-way is cancelled** (`rule:http-server/a-request-outlives-a-client-that-goes-away`): `hyper` keeps that request in flight, so no drop happens. `Supply::pump` sees the `Incoming` error; record whether it `is_incomplete()` and let the service wait cancel a listed method on it — `crates/nvs-server/src/body.rs:181`, `crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs:1730`.

backlog: `nvs-stdlib-a-stream-write-to-a-gone-client-returns`: `Core\Response\Stream::write` after a close and after a send timeout (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/stream.rs`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs`). It is the stage's other red check.
Flip `data/rules/http-server/a-request-outlives-a-client-that-goes-away.json` to `shipped` once the stream write and the group above land.

`wall_time` is published to the tree but nothing enforces it on a served request, attached or detached: a detached request with a `wall_time` is bounded only by the drain. For the user: enforcing it belongs to `rule:http-server/time-is-bounded-inside-a-helper`'s owner, not this goal.

`cancel_on_disconnect`'s `APPLY_PROOFS` row in `crates/nvs-config/tests/directives.rs` names a test that does not read it yet; `a_disconnected_request_of_a_listed_method_is_cancelled` reads it now and can be named there.
